decision: Retain the qualified per-grant coordinator and continue bounded aggregate admission/client service qualification. Preserve existing collectors and live execution.
falsifier: Duplicate dispatch, HTTP before matching admission, lost observed 429, incorrect live-child recovery, fabricated receipt clocks, exposed partial body or failed reproduction reopens the relevant component qualification.
hypothesis: Atomic grant reservation, pre-HTTP child admission and distinct worker observations can prevent duplicate public dispatch and preserve partial failure truth under owner loss.
limitations: Trusted local POSIX process/SQLite/file-lock model; no remote authentication or hard real-time claim.
Per-grant dispatch does not bound aggregate workers, queues or shared-IP weight.
Complete client IPC service, physical workload replay and collector continuity remain pending.
Known raw 429 can be recovered after process death; this is not a completed worker receipt.
No profitability or production request-load benefit is established.
